Hello, this is the final message from the international office before you travel. Three practical things. Your documents: passport, letter of acceptance and medical form go in your hand luggage, never in the suitcase you check in. If your suitcase is delayed, and about one in twenty are, you will still be able to register. Second, the time difference. Vancouver is five hours behind Sao Paulo in September, which sounds small until your family calls you at four in the morning on the first Sunday. Agree a time before you fly. And third, a piece of advice rather than an instruction: say yes to the first three things anybody invites you to, even if you are tired. Especially if you are tired. That is where the whole six months is decided.

Hi Lais, it's Greg. We're all set on this end. Emma has moved her things out of the small room, mostly, and she's already made a list of places she wants to take you, which is longer than the six months you're staying. Two quick things from me. Bring one thing from home that you can cook for us, whatever it is, we're not fussy and we're genuinely curious. And do not worry about the first week. Everybody arrives exhausted and slightly panicked and by the second Saturday it feels normal. We've done this three times now and it has never gone wrong. See you at the airport. I'll have the sign.

Lais makes a checklist and puts her documents in her hand luggage. She agrees a calling time with her family, because of the time difference. On the last evening she says farewell to her friends and to her sister. She lands in Vancouver and finds Greg holding a sign with her name. On the second Saturday the whole thing already feels normal.
